title: The 'Manjummel Boys' Director Is Back, and This Time He's Made Something That Bites. 'Balan: The Boy' Goes From Cannes to Five Languages.
excerpt: Chidambaram, who turned a cave rescue into 2024's most-loved Malayalam blockbuster, returns with a psychological thriller about a mother on the run, a missing past, and a boy hunting for the truth — and the diaspora can catch it in five languages.
body:
The trailer doesn't show you its hand. It shows you a woman with too many names — Mary Luca in one breath, Sherly in the next — and the haunted economy of someone who has spent her whole life looking over her shoulder. A boy clings to her. Police close in from every direction. Somewhere behind them looms a grandmother whose menace the camera only flashes at, like a wound it doesn't want to fully open. By the time the cut comes, you have more questions than answers, and that's exactly the point.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=cjWTqndgZ_M</youtube>

This is **Balan: The Boy**, and it marks the return of one of the most quietly thrilling names in Indian cinema right now: **Chidambaram**. If that name doesn't land immediately, the film behind it will — *Manjummel Boys*, the 2024 survival drama about a group of friends and a near-fatal fall into Kodaikanal's Guna Caves, that became a genuine cultural phenomenon and one of the highest-grossing Malayalam films ever made. Chidambaram took a true story, stripped it of melodrama, and let dread do the work. Audiences across South India and the diaspora didn't just watch it; they couldn't stop talking about it.

https://x.com/LetsXOtt/status/2067883657453510725

Now he's pivoting hard into the dark. **Balan: The Boy** is a psychological thriller, and the script comes from **Jithu Madhavan** — the gleeful chaos engine behind *Romancham* and the riotous *Aavesham*. That pairing is the headline for anyone who follows Malayalam cinema closely: Chidambaram's controlled tension meeting Madhavan's instinct for the unexpected. Two distinct, much-admired storytelling voices in one room is, frankly, the kind of collaboration that makes you sit up.

> "Balan: The Boy is a film about what we carry without knowing — the weight of where we come from, and the hunger to find where we belong. I made this film for the person who has felt both of those things deeply and never found the words for them." — Chidambaram

The story follows a teenage boy whose childhood has been anything but gentle, searching for a mother who has vanished, chasing closure and the truth about a past that keeps slipping away from him. The film stars newcomers **Adhisheshan**, **Farzana Palathingal** and **Muhammad Zinaan** in its central roles, with **Tovino Thomas** — fresh off his own busy run — appearing as Abbas, alongside Jean Paul Lal, Girish A. D. and Beena Antony.

 It's a cast that leans on fresh faces rather than star wattage, which for a thriller about identity and belonging feels like exactly the right instinct.

Behind the camera, Chidambaram has brought much of his *Manjummel Boys* family back: **Sushin Shyam** on music, whose scores have become their own kind of event; cinematographer Shyju Khalid; editor Vivek Harshan; and production designer Ajayan Chalissery. This is a team that already knows how to build unbearable tension out of restraint, and a psychological thriller is the perfect proving ground for that muscle.

The film arrived on the world stage before it ever reached a single Indian multiplex. **Balan: The Boy** screened at the Marché du Film, the official market alongside the **Cannes Film Festival 2026**, where it reportedly drew a warm response from industry buyers and observers. That festival lap matters: it's increasingly how Malayalam cinema announces it isn't a regional curiosity but a force the global film business has to reckon with. Producer Venkat K Narayana of KVN Productions put it bluntly — the film, he said, "is not just a film, it is a statement." When even the men with the spreadsheets start talking like poets, something is in the water.

The support from the wider industry has been telling. **Ajay Devgn**, **Suriya**, **Naga Chaitanya** and Raj B. Shetty all took to social media to push the trailer to their followers — a rare cross-industry show of solidarity that says the people who actually make films believe this one is worth your two-and-a-half hours.

For the diaspora, the access could not be better. **Balan: The Boy** released theatrically on June 19 not only in Malayalam but dubbed into **Hindi, Tamil, Telugu and Kannada** — a five-language rollout that means NRIs from Houston to Toronto to London can find a screening in a language they actually live in, rather than waiting months for a streaming drop. Keep an eye on the usual South Indian theatrical chains abroad, and on the OTT announcement that will inevitably follow a strong theatrical run.

Chidambaram built his reputation on trusting his audience with truth instead of spoon-feeding them spectacle. **Balan: The Boy** looks like the next, darker chapter of that trust. If *Manjummel Boys* was about getting out of the dark, this one looks like it's about learning to live inside it. Either way, the man has earned your ticket.
